label: Damaged object repaired and kept in use
definition: An item matches when its description states both that an existing damaged, broken, bent, torn or leaking object is repaired by an action such as straightening, mending or sealing, and that the same object is kept, used again or remains in use after that repair. An item does not match when its description affirmatively states that the damaged object is discarded or replaced by a different object, or that the described object is newly made from raw material or offcuts rather than an existing object being repaired. When a description does not state whether a repair happened or whether the same object is retained, membership remains unknown; the absence of such a statement is not by itself a reason to exclude the item.
rationale: Three captions state the same two facts: an existing damaged object is repaired, and the same object is kept or remains in use. Item 41001 states that a bent bookmark is straightened and used again and that the existing piece is kept. Item 41002 states that a torn satchel is mended and that the same bag is kept; its phrase about carrying books again is a stated purpose, so the definition does not depend on books actually being carried. Item 41003 states that a leaking jug is sealed and returned to watering plants and that the same jug remains in use. These items sit in three different existing categories (K1, K2 and K3), so this is a new derived group and not a renamed old category. Other captions describe replacement with a newly purchased object, making new objects from offcuts or a raw blank, or give no activity, so they do not supply support for this definition. This is a proposal only; a user must review it before any classification.
alternatives: A broader meaning of keeping material in use instead of acquiring something new, which would include making a new object from leftover material such as paper offcuts as well as repairing an existing object; this is a different concept from repairing and keeping the same object.
A meaning centred on the method of work, namely hand work done without powered equipment, which would group objects by the tools used rather than by whether an existing object is repaired and kept.

evidence.quote: A bent metal bookmark is straightened with pliers and used again. The existing piece is kept.
evidence.reason: States that an existing bent object is straightened (repaired) and used again, and that the existing piece is kept, which supports both conditions of the definition.

evidence.quote: A torn canvas satchel is mended with a needle and spare thread so it can carry books again. The same bag is kept.
evidence.reason: States that an existing torn object is mended (repaired) and that the same bag is kept, which supports both conditions; carrying books again is only a stated purpose and is not used as evidence that it happened.

evidence.quote: A leaking clay jug is sealed and returned to watering plants. The same jug remains in use.
evidence.reason: States that an existing leaking object is sealed (repaired) and that the same jug remains in use, which supports both conditions of the definition.
